description: Rhythm and position rules JSON Schema cannot express. Each rule is implemented in schema/semantic_validate.py (RULES) under the same id; extraction/verify_all.py checks the two agree and that every real template satisfies every rule apart from the named exceptions.

rules.description: The first node is the page navigation shell (site header, landing-page-only nav, or the dive gallery app nav).

exceptions.reason: The /try app renders no site chrome (App.jsx BARE_PATHS); its single node is the whole static app shell.

rules.description: The last node is the page footer shell (site footer or the dive gallery footer).

exceptions.reason: The book landing page hides the site header and footer (extra-marketing.css lines 97-100) and ends with its gated form.

rules.description: At most one HERO (page-opening composition) per page. The product-feature opener group offers two alternatives of which exactly one is used.

When a page has a HERO it is the first non-shell node. Pages without a HERO (article, legal, form and index-style pages) are allowed; they are listed in params.heroOptionalTemplates, derived from templates.json.
Two blocks of the same persuasion category (FAQ, SOCIAL_PROOF, CTA, CONVERSION) are not stacked directly. Feature, listing, editorial and navigation blocks legitimately repeat and are not restricted.

exceptions.reason: Measured order in StartupsPage: quote spotlight, then investor logos.
Measured order in About.jsx: contact band, then community call-to-action.
The registration sidebar sits in the article row directly above the newsletter band (EventDetail.jsx).

rules.description: Two sections that scrub on scroll (sticky-stack-scrub, story-scale-scrub) are not adjacent.
A (section, variant) pair appears once unless the template node is repeatable. One section may appear twice with different variants (the quote card on the homepage).
Runtime UI (modals, drawers, floating and fixed bars, skip link, scroll effects) is listed in template.runtimeUi and never composed as a page node.
Number of sections whose motion is a continuous infinite loop. The ceiling is the largest count found in a real template (computed from templates.json and the contracts at write time).
Per-section constraints from the contracts: onePerPage, maxPerPage, minPerPage, mustBeFirst, mustBeLast, mustFollowNav, mustPrecedeFooter.
